text: Most roles you'd assign for Data Factory are standard, built-in Azure roles — Owner, Contributor, Reader. There's exactly one Data Factory-specific role genuinely worth knowing by name: Data Factory Contributor.

Here's the detail that trips people up: Contributor is genuinely a superset of Data Factory Contributor. If someone already has Contributor at the resource group level, granting them Data Factory Contributor too does nothing extra at all. Data Factory Contributor exists for the narrower case — managing factories and their child resources without blanket rights across every other resource type.

The exact same role means something different depending on where you assign it. Data Factory Contributor at the resource group level can create, edit, and delete any factory in that group. Contributor scoped to one individual factory can edit that single resource but genuinely can't create new ones or touch anything else. Assign at the narrowest scope that still does the job.

Here's a real, specific scenario worth internalizing: Git repo permissions and Data Factory permissions are genuinely independent of each other. A user who's only a Data Factory Reader, but has write access to the connected repo, can edit child resources and commit changes — but can't click Publish. A genuinely useful way to let someone stage changes for review without pushing straight to the live factory.

Two built-in roles, a scope decision that changes everything, and a genuinely useful can-edit-can't-publish pattern built on the independence of Git and factory permissions.
